==English== {{wp|,Path (graph theory)}} [[File:Muybridge horse walking animated.gif|thumb|right|A horse walking.]] ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|UK}} ** {{IPA|en|/wɔːk/|a=RP}} ** {{IPA|en|/woːk/|a=SSBE}} *** {{audio|en|en-uk-walk.ogg|a=SSB}} ** {{IPA|en|/waːk/|a=Northumbria}} ** {{IPA|en|/wɔk/|a=Scotland}} * {{a|en|US}} ** {{enPR|wôk|a=non-cot-caught}}, {{IPA|en|/wɔk/}} ** {{enPR|wäk|a=cot-caught}}, {{IPA|en|/wɑk/}} *** {{audio|en|en-us-walk.ogg|a=US,cot-caught}} * {{IPA|en|/woːk/|a=AU,NZ}} ** {{audio|en|en-au-walk.ogg|a=AU}} * {{homophones|en|wok|aa=cot-caught}} * {{rhymes|en|ɔːk|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*welH-}} From {{inh|en|enm|walk}}, {{m|enm|walke}}, {{m|enm|walken}}, {{m|enm|walkyn}}, {{m|enm|wolken|t=to roll, toss, or turn; to walk; to move; to be living; to beat or full; to perform}}, a conflation of {{inh|en|ang|wealcan|t=to move around; to revolve; to roll; to fluctuate; to discuss}} ({{m|ang|ġewealcan|t=to go, traverse; to roll}}) and {{inh|en|ang|wealcian|t=to curl, roll up, twist; to wrinkle}}; both from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*walkan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*walkaną|t=to roll, toss, turn, wind; to walk, wander, wend; to full, trample}}, {{m|gem-pro|*walkōną|t=to roll about; to full}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*walg-|t=to twist, turn, move}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|bar|woikn|t=to full, tan; to knead dough; to roll out dough}}, {{cog|cim|balchan|t=to beat, hit, strike}}, {{cog|nl|zwalken|t=to walk around}}, {{cog|de|walken|t=to full, tan, walk; to knead; to beat up}}, {{cog|da|valke|t=to full, walk, waulk}}, {{cog|fo|válka|t=make dirty; stir up dirt}}, {{cog|sv|valka|t=to full cloth, to waulk}}; also {{cog|la|valgus|t=bent out; bandy, bow-legged}}. More at {{l|en|vagrant}} and {{l|en|whelk}}. Doublet of {{l|en|waulk}}. {{col-bottom}} ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|walke||obsolete}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[move]] on the [[feet]] by [[alternately]] [[setting]] each [[foot]] (or pair or group of feet: in the case of some non-human [[animals]] with four or more feet) [[forward]], with at least one foot on the [[ground]] at all times. Compare '''[[run]]'''. #: {{ux|en|To '''walk''' briskly for an hour every day is to keep fit.}} #* {{RQ:Besant Ivory Gate|chapter=Prologue|page=16|passage=Athelstan Arundel walked home all the way, foaming and raging. {{...}} His mother lived at Pembridge Square, which is four good measured miles from Lincoln's Inn. He walked the whole way, '''walking''' through crowds, and under the noses of dray-horses, carriage-horses, and cart-horses, without taking the least notice of them.}} #* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=XXXIII|page=257|passage=Edward Churchill still attended to his work in a hopeless mechanical manner like a sleep-walker who '''walks''' safely on a well-known round. But his Roman collar galled him, his cossack stifled him, his biretta was as uncomfortable as a merry-andrew's cap and bells.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|colloquial|legal}} To "[[walk free]]", i.e. to win, or avoid, a criminal court case, particularly when [[actually]] [[guilty]]. #: {{ux|en|If you can’t present a better case, that robber is going to '''walk'''.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|colloquial|euphemistic}} Of an object, to go [[missing]] or be [[stolen]]. #: {{ux|en|If you leave your wallet lying around, it’s going to '''walk'''.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|cricket|of a batsman}} To walk off the field, as if [[given]] [[out]], after the [[fielding]] [[side]] [[appeal]]s and before the [[umpire]] has [[ruled]]; done as a matter of [[sportsmanship]] when the batsman believes he is out. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To travel (a distance) by walking. #: {{ux|en|I '''walk''' two miles to school every day.}} #: {{ux|en|The museum’s not far from here – you can '''walk''' it.}} #* {{RQ:Besant Ivory Gate|chapter=Prologue|page=16|passage=Athelstan Arundel '''walked''' home all the way, foaming and raging. {{...}} His mother lived at Pembridge Square, which is four good measured miles from Lincoln's Inn. He '''walked''' the whole way, walking through crowds, and under the noses of dray-horses, carriage-horses, and cart-horses, without taking the least notice of them.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To take for a walk or accompany on a walk. #: {{ux|en|I '''walk''' the dog every morning.}} #: {{ux|en|Will you '''walk''' me home?}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merry Wives|act=II|scene=ii|page=47|passage=I will rather trust{{...}}a thief to '''walk''' my ambling gelding.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|with ''in''}} To appear in a [[parade]]. #: {{ux|en|Those who wish to '''walk''' in the parade this fall should sign up now.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|baseball}} To allow a batter to reach base by [[pitch]]ing four [[ball|balls]]. # {{lb|en|intransitive|baseball|of a|batter}} To reach base by being pitched four balls. # {{lb|en|intransitive}} Of an object or machine, to move by [[shifting]] between two positions, as if it were walking. #: {{ux|en|If we don't bolt the washing machine down, it's going to '''walk''' across the room.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause something to move in such a way. #: {{ux|en|I carefully '''walked''' the ladder along the wall.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[full]]; to [[beat]] (cloth) to give it the consistency of [[felt]]. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[traverse]] by walking (or analogous gradual movement). #: {{ux|en|I '''walked''' the streets aimlessly.}} #: {{ux|en|Debugging this computer program involved '''walking''' the heap.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|aviation}} To operate the left and right [[throttle]]s of (an aircraft) in alternation. # {{lb|en|intransitive|colloquial}} To leave, resign. #: {{ux|en|If we don't offer him more money he'll '''walk'''.}} #* {{RQ:Spenser Ireland|page=39|passage=He will make their cowes and garrans to '''walk'''.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To push (a vehicle) alongside oneself as one walks. # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To behave; to pursue a course of life; to conduct oneself. #* {{RQ:Taylor Holy Living}}, [https://books.google.com/books?id=xIVmAAAAcAAJ&pg=PA35 page 35] # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To go restlessly about; said of things or persons expected to remain quiet, such as a sleeping person, or the spirit of a dead person. #* '''October 9, 1550''', {{w|Hugh Latimer}}, ''sermon preached at Stamford'', [https://books.google.com/books?id=R-pCAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA94 link] # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To be in motion; to act; to move. #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|year=1590|book=II|canto=IV|stanza=5|page=233|passage=her toung did '''walke''' / In fowle reproch.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Winter's Tale|act=III|scene=iii|page=288|passage=I have heard, but not believed, the spirits of the dead / May '''walk''' again.}} #* {{RQ:Jonson [[dogfighting]]. # {{lb|en|informal|transitive}} To move (a guest) to another [[hotel]] if their [[confirmed]] [[reservation]] is not [[available]] on the day of [[check-in]]. # {{senseid|en|of a tool, to wander}} {{lb|en|machining|intransitive|of a tool, such as a [[drill bit]] or [[reamer]]}} To tend to move radially while feeding axially, whether tending toward on-center or tending toward Cognate with {{cog|is|volk|t=difficulty, hardship, trouble}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # A trip made by walking. #: {{ux|en|I take a '''walk''' every morning.}} #: {{co|en|go on a '''walk'''}} #* {{quote-journal |en |year=1894 |title=From Month to Month |url=https://archive.org/details/chronicleoflond1894lond_7/ |journal=The Chronicle of the {{w|London Missionary Society}} |issue=33 |publisher=Readers Union |oclc=183334441 |page=220 |pageurl=https://archive.org/details/chronicleoflond1894lond_7/page/220/ |text=FOUR BAPTISMS IN YING-SHAN
We had looked forward to four or five days' work in Ying-shan similar to that in Yün-mung,but at the end of our two days' '''walk''' from the one city to the other (they lie more than fifty miles apart), Mr. Terrell had a touch of fever, so we judged it best to remain in Ying-shan only for a day and then travel as quickly as possible by chair to Teh-ngan to consult our good friend, Dr. Morley, of the Wesleyan Mission Hospital in that city, and from thence take boat for Hankow.}} # A distance walked. #: {{ux|en|It’s a long '''walk''' from my house to the library.}} #: {{ux|en|The precinct is about ten minutes’ '''walk''', [[straight ahead]], so you can’t miss it.}} # {{lb|en|sports}} An Olympic Games track event requiring that the heel of the leading foot touch the ground before the toe of the trailing foot leaves the ground. # A manner of walking; a person's style of walking. #: {{ux|en|The Ministry of Silly '''Walks''' is underfunded this year.}} # A path, [[sidewalk]]/[[pavement]] or other maintained place on which to walk. #: {{cot|en|trail}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1902|author=John Buchan|title=The Outgoing of the Tide |passage=And then it appeared to the young man that he was walking his love up the grass '''walk''' of Heriotside, with the house close by him.}} # {{lb|en|figurative}} A person's [[conduct]] or [[course]] in [[life]]. #: {{uxi|en|people of different ages and '''walks'''}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1887|author=Sir Thomas Henry Hall Caine; Sir Hall Caine; John Parker Anderson|title=Life of Samuel Taylor Coleridge|page=136 |passage=Men like Stuart who had no desire to extol Coleridge's virtues, and other witnesses quite as hostile, to whom a moral dereliction could hardly be a mortal offence, were loud in praise of the purity of his '''walk''' in life.}} # {{lb|en|poker}} A situation where all players [[fold]] to the [[big blind]], as their first [[action]] (instead of [[call]]ing or [[raise|raising]]), once they get their [[card]]s. # {{senseid|en|baseball}} {{lb|en|baseball}} An award of first base to a batter following four balls being thrown by the pitcher; known in the rules as a "base on balls". #: {{ux|en|The pitcher now has two '''walks''' in this inning alone.}} # In [[coffee]], [[coconut]], and other [[plantation]]s, the space between them. # {{lb|en|Caribbean|Belize|Guyana|Jamaica}} An area of an [[estate]] planted with fruit-bearing trees.Lise Winer (ed.), ''Dictionary of the English/Creole of Trinidad and Tobago'', McGill-Queen’s University Press, 2008, p.{{nbsp}}940.[https://books.google.ca/books?id=_n82hsbDJBMC&printsec=frontcover#v=onepage&q&f=false] #* {{quote-book|en|year=1755|author=William Belgrove|title=A Treatise upon Husbandry or Planting|location=Boston|page=14|url=https://archive.org/details/treatiseuponhusb00belg |passage=Twenty Acres of Land well kept in a Plantain '''Walk''', will afford a very considerable Support, as Plantains are as hearty a Food as [[eddoe|Eddoes]], and the Plantain '''Walk''' may be a Nursery for declining Slaves, as well as to fatten old Cattle when they are past Labour.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1803|author=w:Robert Charles Dallas|title=The History of the Maroons|location=London|publisher=Longman and Rees|section=Volume 1, Letter 4, [https://archive.org/details/cihm_44228/page/n224/mode/1up page 80] |passage=For half a mile from Vaughansfield the road, now a mere track, leads through pastures and a coffee-'''walk''' to the foot of a very steep hill {{...}}}} #* '''1961''', {{w|Wilson Harris}}, ''The Far Journey of Oudin'', Book 2, Chapter 6, in ''The Guyana Quartet'', London: Faber and Faber, 1985, p.{{nbsp}}150,[https://archive.org/details/guyanaquartet00harr] #* {{quote-book|en|year=1995|author=w:Olive Senior|chapter=Window|title=Discerner of Hearts|location=Toronto|publisher=McClelland & Stewart|page=66|url=https://archive.org/details/discernerofheart00oliv |passage=He couldn’t sleep and took to walking outside at night, to look at the stars, to feel the cool air, and for a long time wasn’t even conscious that he always ended up standing in the darkness of the cocoa '''walk''' staring at the shutters of Bridget’s room.}} #
